name: What size garage can be converted into an ADU without major redesign?

mainEntity.name: Is a one-car garage enough for a legal ADU, or do you need a two-car garage to make the layout work in Los Angeles-area homes?
mainEntity.text: Is a one-car garage enough for a legal ADU, or do you need a two-car garage to make the layout work in Los Angeles-area homes?

acceptedAnswer.text: Garage size strongly affects what kind of ADU you can build. A one-car garage may work for a studio or very compact one-bedroom layout, but it can become tight once you account for kitchen clearances, bathroom dimensions, mechanical equipment, and required circulation. Two-car garages generally give designers more freedom to create a livable floor plan with better storage and natural light. The existing structure also matters: ceiling height, slab condition, wall framing, and door placement can either simplify or complicate the conversion. Homeowners should not assume that square footage alone determines feasibility. A well-designed smaller garage can outperform a larger but awkward one. Before committing to a layout, ask for furniture placement, code clearances, and utility routing on the plans so the finished unit does not feel cramped or expensive to correct later.
acceptedAnswer.description: A one-car garage can often become a compact ADU, but layout efficiency, ceiling height, plumbing routing, and code-required circulation determine whether the conversion is practical. Two-car garages usually offer more flexibility for a bedroom, kitchen, bathroom, and storage without extreme space compromises.
